summary.verdict: This is already a stronger regulatory page than anything in the casebook on structure: the system is split into three components, every classification is hedged, and a whole section lists what is still unconfirmed. It falls behind the winners on people and on proof. One industry briefing stands in for all stakeholders, no regulator was asked anything, no rule is cited by article, and no design change on the page is traced to a rule. Several claims also disagree with the Entrepreneurship and Geospatial Analysis pages, which is the fastest way to lose a judge's trust on legal writing.
strengths: The three-component split (bioreactor, culture, cell-free output), held consistently from section 1 to section 9.
Honest hedging: "a potential pathway for ReLeaf's cell-free output, but not an automatic classification", and a review that says what it could not find.
Section 10, which lists every unconfirmed item in one table instead of hiding them.
Kelpak and Sagarika as real products that show classification changing by place and by time.
The sentence that ties engineering to law: containment determines the exposure pathway regulators must consider.
Figure 3's caption, which names the source, her title, the date and how the information was used.
40 C.F.R. Part 725 cited where the claim is made, and the Taiwanese category given in Chinese and English.
priorities: Fix the page-to-page contradictions first: the market order and the 30-day fertilizer timeline against Entrepreneurship, Taiwan contained-use against Entrepreneurship's "absolute containment" certification, ACCD heat against the salinity evidence on Geospatial Analysis, the organic exclusion against Geospatial Analysis, the missing NaD1, and BoPEP4 against BoPep4.

Turn section 8 into a real stakeholder entry, and add at least one regulator and one critic. Ask the two questions WageningenUR asked: does each molecule need its own approval, and what residual cell or DNA limit applies to the output.

Name one design change that a rule caused, and write it where a judge will see it. Your Human Practices page already records the move away from direct soil release; that is a legal decision and it belongs here with a link.
Cite rules by article with a link and an access date, and give every unconfirmed item an owner and a next step.
Cut the repetition: the abstract is restated in section 2, the molecule list appears six times, the Kelpak table is retold in prose, and "rather than" carries 18 sentences.
Summarise this page in one line with a link on Human Practices, Safety and Sustainability. Judges only reach it from pages with a Standard URL, and today only Entrepreneurship names it.

ballot.question: How well was the Human Practices work integrated throughout the project?
ballot.where: 2. Regulation as product design; 4. Function to claim to classification
ballot.note: The page argues that regulation shaped the build, and Table 1 states it as a principle, but no single design decision on the page is traced to a named rule.

ballot.question: How inspiring an example is it to others?
ballot.where: 3. Three components, three regulatory questions; 10. Exploring the ambiguity
ballot.note: The component split and the unconfirmed table are reusable by any team with a contained production system; the research method behind them is never described.

ballot.question: To what extent is the Human Practices work documented so that others can build upon it?
ballot.note: Eleven markets with named instruments is real documentation, but no claim carries an article number, links are bare domains, and nothing has an access date.

ballot.question: How thoughtfully was it implemented? How well did they explain the context, rationale and prior work?
ballot.where: 4.1 EU reference point; 7. What existing products teach us; 9. Where does ReLeaf sit?
ballot.note: Prior work arrives as two comparable products, and the rationale chain from function to market access is stated and then followed.

ballot.question: How well did it incorporate different stakeholder views?
ballot.note: One industry briefing, with the name only in a figure caption. No regulator, no lawyer, no organic farmer and no critic of GM agriculture appears.

releaf: 4. Function to claim to classification (4.1 EU reference point)
7. What existing products teach us (Kelpak, Sagarika)
10. Exploring the ambiguity (what is still unconfirmed?)
winners: Open with the questions the page answers, or with the rule that is about to change the design
One entry per rule, five slots each: the rule, what it requires, what it means for a named component, who confirmed it, what the team changed
A comparable product already on the market as the anchor for the argument
Unresolved classifications written as conditionals, with a date and a status
The design change repeated on the lab, hardware or business page it changed
A one-line summary and a link on every page that has a Standard URL
skeleton.gap: Your skeleton is built by jurisdiction and component, which the winners never manage, and it reads well. What it has no room for is the entry: a named person, the question you asked, the answer, and the change that followed. Sections 8 and 10 are where those entries belong, and both currently stop before the person and the change.

extras: "Regulation is therefore not the final checkpoint of ReLeaf - it is one of the constraints that shape what we build" is the third time section 2 says this. Cut the sentence.
The three bullets in section 8 ("Product classification should be considered early." and the two after it) repeat Table 1's three principles. Replace them with what Yuan Chiu-Ying actually told you.
"Our goal is not simply to identify a legal category after the product is built" repeats sections 1 and 2 again. Keep one closing sentence.
The table in section 4 heads its first column "Biostimulant" although the paragraph above says no authority has classified the molecules. Rename the column "Molecule".
Headings run together: "1.Abstract", "4.1EU reference point". Put a space after each number.
"Cheng Han Biotechnology's Break Down of Different Global Market's Legal Authorities." Breakdown is one word, and it should be "Markets' Legal Authorities".
"Table 1. Three Principles Shaped Our Development" reads as a half sentence. Write "Table 1. Three principles that shaped our development."
"#### Cell-free output" is used as a heading under both Taiwan and the United States. Add the market to each one.

"'Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations Part 725'" does not need the quotation marks. Drop them, and cite Section 725.424 where you mention the exemption, since it is already in your references.

In the Malaysia row, "Fertilizer inputs are subject to agricultural and product-control requirements, but the exact route for ReLeaf's formulation requires further investigation" sits in the pathway column and answers the next column. Split it between the two.
The references name the same body twice: "Environmental Protection Agency. (2020)." and "U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. (2025)." Use one form.

"Developed by IFFCO, Sagarika is a microbial biostimulant". Check this against the Fertilizer Control Order source you cite; if Sagarika is seaweed-derived like Kelpak, say so, because your comparison of the two cases depends on it.
Figure 4 labels the Taiwanese category "plant auxiliary products" while the text calls it "植物生長輔助劑類 (Plant Growth Auxiliary Materials)". Use one label in both places.

The four United States questions are listed, then only three get an answer; "Which state-level fertilizer or beneficial-substance requirements apply?" never gets its own paragraph. Answer all four in the order you asked them.

notes.anchor: We examined how each component is treated in Taiwan, the European Union, the United States
notes.title: The page opens with its scope
notes.body: Your first two sentences split ReLeaf into three parts and name the four places you checked. A judge reads one line and knows what the page covers and how it is organised. Most law pages open with general sentences about regulation and never say what they examined.

notes.anchor: with Taiwan as the development environment and the EU as our current first international market
notes.title: Market order disagrees with Entrepreneurship
notes.body: Here the EU is "our current first international market to investigate". The Entrepreneurship page puts the European Union in "Global market expansion Year 5.5 - Year 6.0+" and makes the Philippines the first expansion in year 3. Pick one order and write the same one on both pages.
notes.after: with Taiwan as the development environment and the EU as the first market we studied in depth. Our planned market order is [order], the same order given on the Entrepreneurship page.
notes.excerpt_note: WageningenUR repeats the same regulatory figure and the same source on its business page, so the two pages agree.

notes.anchor: We examined these components across Taiwan, the European Union, the United States
notes.title: This paragraph repeats the abstract
notes.body: Section 2 opens by saying again what section 1 just said, almost word for word. Cut it and start section 2 with the chain that follows, which is new.
notes.after: Our regulatory analysis follows: Function - Claim - Classification - Requirement - Market Access.

notes.anchor: Abiotic-stress positioning makes fertilizer/biostimulant pathways the main strategy under investigation
notes.title: Say the principle in plain words
notes.body: "Abiotic-stress positioning" is your own shorthand, and a judge often reads the table before the prose. Write the principle as cause and effect.
notes.after: Because we claim stress tolerance and no pest control, the fertilizer and biostimulant routes are our main strategy.

notes.anchor: The regulatory information from this briefing was used as an industry perspective
notes.title: This caption sources itself properly
notes.body: The caption names the researcher, her title, her company, the date of the briefing, and what you did with what she said. It also marks the briefing as an industry view beside your primary sources. A judge can check every part of that.
notes.excerpt_note: WageningenUR names the regulator's staff, the question asked and the answer in the same paragraph.
notes.ballot: How well did it incorporate different stakeholder views?

notes.anchor: separately assesses GMO/GMM transport, storage, and waste requirements
notes.title: Write out GMM once
notes.body: GMO is expanded nowhere on the page and GMM appears only here. An international judge may know GMO and not GMM. Give both in full the first time.
notes.after: Keeps the culture inside the production system, and separately assesses transport, storage and waste rules for genetically modified organisms and micro-organisms (GMOs and GMMs).

notes.anchor: Containment is not only an engineering requirement; it determines the exposure pathway
notes.title: One sentence carries the whole argument
notes.body: This sentence ties your hardware to the law: containment decides what a regulator has to consider. Everything later on the page depends on it, and you state it once, clearly. Keep it where it is.

notes.anchor: also allows the two components be assessed as distinct regulatory questions
notes.title: Missing word in the last sentence
notes.body: It should read "to be assessed". The sentence is also long. Split it.
notes.after: Separating the engineered production organism from the cell-free output lets regulators assess the two as distinct questions.

notes.anchor: The hollow-fiber membrane forms part of this separation
notes.title: Name the detail that decides containment
notes.body: You say the membrane holds the culture back, but not what a regulator would measure. Give the pore size, say whether live cells or DNA can leave with the output, and name the limit you would have to meet. Link to Safety and Hardware, where the evidence sits.
notes.after: The hollow-fiber membrane ([pore size]) retains the production culture and lets the soluble products through. No live cells leave the loop, and residual DNA in the output is [number], measured as described on our Safety page.
notes.excerpt_note: Marburg found the one design detail (a 34 bp scar) that decides its legal category. WageningenUR asked its regulator for the residual DNA threshold and got 0.9%, dead or alive cells.
notes.ballot: To what extent is the Human Practices work documented so that others can build upon it?

notes.anchor: The three molecules are treated as biostimulants
notes.title: Two hedges in one paragraph
notes.body: This paragraph hedges the word biostimulant twice and in three long sentences. Say it once, in two short ones. The table below also heads its first column "Biostimulant", which undoes the hedge; call that column "Molecule".
notes.after: We call these three molecules biostimulants because of what they do in the plant. No authority has classified them, so the column below gives the category we are aiming at.

notes.anchor: Our intended function is therefore abiotic-stress resilience rather than control of pathogens, insects, or weeds
notes.title: NaD1 is missing from this page
notes.body: The Entrepreneurship page lists NaD1 (antifungal defence) as one of the three proteins the bioreactor makes, and plans a "biopesticide designation for NaD1". Your page names three molecules and rules out pathogen claims. Say what happened to NaD1: dropped, or kept with a separate pesticide route.
notes.after: Our intended function is abiotic-stress resilience. We make no claim about pathogens, insects or weeds. [NaD1 is no longer part of the product / NaD1 would need a separate pesticide route, described in section [n]].

notes.anchor: This makes PFC 6(B) a potential pathway for ReLeaf
notes.title: A pathway named without claiming it
notes.body: You name a route and then refuse to claim it. The difference between a possible route and an approval is exactly what a judge checks on a law page, and you mark it.
notes.excerpt_note: Waterloo writes the same uncertainty as an if-then sentence, which is the shape you could use for your Taiwan paragraphs too.

notes.anchor: PFC 6(B) covers non-microbial plant biostimulants
notes.title: Explain why a cell-free output is non-microbial
notes.body: PFC 6(B) is for non-microbial biostimulants, and your product is made by a micro-organism. A reader will stop here. Give the reason in one sentence, and say what cell or DNA limit you would have to meet.
notes.after: PFC 6(B) covers non-microbial plant biostimulants. Our output contains no cells, so we are investigating it under PFC 6(B), which would require us to show no live cells and no more than [limit] residual DNA.
notes.excerpt_note: This is the question WageningenUR put to RIVM, and the answer it got back decided their downstream processing.

notes.anchor: current biostimulants are being investigated for complementary abiotic-stress functions
notes.title: The molecule list appears six times
notes.body: BoPep4 for salinity, AtLEA14 for drought and ACCD for heat are listed in sections 4, 4.1, Taiwan, EU, 9, 10 and 11. Give the list once in the table in section 4 and refer back to it after that.
notes.after: The three molecules are being investigated for the abiotic-stress functions in Table [n]. The final product must also satisfy applicable composition, safety, efficacy, labeling, and conformity requirements.

notes.anchor: Taiwan is our development and validation environment.
notes.title: Say what you actually do in Taiwan
notes.body: "Development and validation environment" tells a judge very little. Name the work: the lab, the plant trials, the farmer meetings, and the first registration.
notes.after: Taiwan is where we build and test ReLeaf. Our lab work, plant trials and farmer meetings are all here, and it is where we would register first.

notes.anchor: fertilizer specifications recognize 植物生長輔助劑類 (Plant Growth Auxiliary Materials) among its fertilizer categories
notes.title: You give the Taiwanese term both ways
notes.body: The Chinese category name with an English translation lets a judge outside Taiwan search the real term, and a Taiwanese reader see the exact wording. Do this for every Taiwanese law and category you name.

notes.anchor: The final formulation and claims would need to be characterized and confirmed with the Ministry of Agriculture.
notes.title: Name the agencies and their laws
notes.body: Judges from other countries do not know how Taiwan's Ministry of Agriculture is split. Your Figure 2 has the answer, so put it in the text once, before you rely on it.
notes.after: Taiwan's Ministry of Agriculture oversees both routes. The Agriculture and Food Agency registers fertilizers under the Fertilizer Management Act, and the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency handles pesticides under the Pesticide Management Act. We would confirm our formulation and claims with the Agriculture and Food Agency.
notes.excerpt_note: Marburg says who sets a rule and who decides the details, which is what a reader needs before the rule itself.

notes.anchor: If registered as a fertilizer, ReLeaf would need to establish a defined and reproducible product composition
notes.title: Timeline disagrees with Entrepreneurship
notes.body: Your page says the category still needs confirmation from the Ministry of Agriculture. The Entrepreneurship page says the fertilizer route takes "approximately 20 days for fertilizer specification report plus 7 days for government review" and brings "early revenue within 30 days". Both cannot be true. Carry the same durations and the same source onto both pages.
notes.after: If registered as a fertilizer, ReLeaf would need a defined and reproducible composition, safety and quality data, efficacy data, labeling and registration information. [Name] told us the review itself takes about [number] days once the file is complete.
notes.excerpt_note: WageningenUR's 2.5 to 3.5 year approval figure appears on the IHP page and the business timeline with the same attribution.
notes.ballot: How well was the Human Practices work integrated throughout the project?

notes.anchor: Our current review did not identify a general Taiwan contained-use GMO framework
notes.title: You say what you could not find
notes.body: You report a gap in your own research instead of guessing. This is the most honest line on the page, and it costs nothing. Keep the sentence and add the date of the review.
notes.excerpt_note: UZurich states plainly that its product could not be used in its own country. Judges rewarded that page.

notes.anchor: We therefore treat its regulatory status as unconfirmed.
notes.title: Entrepreneurship promises what this page cannot find
notes.body: This page finds no Taiwan contained-use framework that resolves your case. The Entrepreneurship page says "Taiwan's regulatory framework contains a critical pathway: if engineered bacteria never leave the sealed device, the system can be classified as contained-use equipment", and expects "absolute containment" certification by the end of year 2. One page says the route is not there, the other sells a certificate from it. Fix both.
notes.after: We therefore treat its regulatory status as unconfirmed. Before commercial deployment we would ask [agency] whether a sealed system counts as contained use, which is the question our business plan depends on.

notes.anchor: The bioreactor is an equipment rather than the agricultural product itself.
notes.title: Equipment is uncountable here
notes.body: Write "is equipment", with no "an". You could also make the sentence do more work.
notes.after: The bioreactor is equipment, and not the agricultural product itself.

notes.anchor: heat-stress mitigation evidence for ACCD
notes.title: ACCD is tested on salt elsewhere
notes.body: Here ACCD carries the heat claim. The Geospatial Analysis page reports ACCD evidence under salt stress, "holding onto 86.3% of unstressed performance at moderate salinity". If your ACCD data is salinity data, the claim you can support today is salinity. Match the claim to the experiment on every page, and link to Results.
notes.after: The intended claim decides the evidence we need. Our ACCD data so far is [salinity / heat] data, reported on our Results page, and the [other] claim still has no supporting experiment.

notes.anchor: For ReLeaf, the main question remain:
notes.title: Plural verb and a missing word
notes.body: Three questions follow, so it should read "the main questions remain". There are four bullets under it, not three.
notes.after: For ReLeaf, four questions remain:

notes.anchor: 40 C.F.R. Part 725) is a principal federal framework to investigate
notes.title: You cite the law where you use it
notes.body: This is the one place on the page where the instrument and the part number sit next to the claim. No winner page in our casebook does that. Do the same for your EU and Taiwan claims, with the article number and a link.
notes.excerpt_note: Waterloo puts a numbered source on each sentence of its regulator paragraph.

notes.anchor: No single harmonized federal biostimulant pathway
notes.title: This table needs a title and a home
notes.body: The EU and US comparison arrives with no caption, no header on its first column, and no Taiwan column, and it sits under the "Equipment" heading as if it belonged to the United States. Give it a number and a title, label the first column, add Taiwan, and move it to the end of section 5.
notes.after: Table [n]. The three target markets compared. First column: Topic. Then Taiwan, European Union, United States.

notes.anchor: After Taiwan and the EU, ReLeaf would investigate selected Southeast Asian markets
notes.title: Expansion table mixes two lists
notes.body: The table under this sentence is headed by priority, yet priority 1 is Taiwan, your development environment, and the EU is missing although your sequence puts it second. Start the table at the Philippines and keep Taiwan and the EU in section 5.
notes.after: After Taiwan and the EU, we would enter selected Southeast Asian markets one at a time. The table ranks those markets; Taiwan and the EU are covered in section 5.

notes.anchor: The horizontal axis represents the clarity with which ReLeaf could identify the competent authority
notes.title: Caption does not match the chart
notes.body: The chart's own axes are labelled regulatory and commercialization challenge, and strategic market value for ReLeaf. Your caption describes different axes, and it names five markets while the table lists eleven. Rewrite the caption to match the figure. The last sentence, which says the positions are your own synthesis, is the right kind of honesty and should stay.
notes.after: Figure 7. Five expansion markets placed by regulatory and commercialization challenge (horizontal) against strategic value for ReLeaf (vertical). The positions are our qualitative synthesis of the frameworks we reviewed, not official ratings or approval predictions.

notes.anchor: Fertilizer regulation exists, but current market and regulatory conditions require further investigation
notes.title: Six rows say the same thing
notes.body: Rows 6 to 11 all say a fertilizer framework exists and the exact route needs investigation. Keep rows 1 to 5, which carry your priorities, and replace the rest with one sentence.
notes.after: Malaysia, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Singapore and Brunei all have fertilizer registration systems, and each would need its own check of product category and GMO requirements. We placed them below our priority markets because of [reason].

notes.anchor: This sequence is based on regulatory fit and development readiness rather than market size alone.
notes.title: Eighteen sentences turn on one phrase
notes.body: "rather than" appears 18 times on this page. Readers start to hear the same sentence shape every paragraph. Change most of them to a plain statement.
notes.after: We ranked this sequence by regulatory fit and development readiness, not by market size.

notes.anchor: Kelpak provides a useful case study for understanding why ReLeaf cannot assume
notes.title: A real product anchors the argument
notes.body: You take one product already on the market and show it treated three ways in three places. That proves your point about classification better than any general statement, and it gives a judge something checkable.
notes.excerpt_note: Marburg compares countries on one concrete measure, which is the same move: one thing, several jurisdictions.

notes.anchor: In the European Union, Kelpak is positioned within the EU fertilising-products framework
notes.title: These paragraphs retell the table
notes.body: The Kelpak table already gives each market, its treatment and what it shows. The two paragraphs after it say the same three things in longer form. Keep the table, cut the retelling, and end with your conclusion.
notes.after: The table shows the pattern: Kelpak does not change when it crosses a border, but its pathway does. We therefore treat each target market as a separate regulatory assessment.

notes.anchor: For ReLeaf, this reinforces the importance of establishing product identity
notes.title: Duplicate sentence after Sagarika
notes.body: The paragraph above already says this, with "defining" in place of "establishing". Cut one of the two.
notes.after: (Delete this line; the same point is made inside the paragraph above.)

notes.anchor: Our exchange with Cheng Han Biotechnology supplemented our legal research with industry experience
notes.title: Write the briefing as a full entry
notes.body: This is your only stakeholder on the page, and the section gives no name, no question and no change. Figure 3 already has the name and the date. Write the five parts: who you asked, what you asked, what she said, what it means for which component, and what you changed. Add the meeting to the Human Practices page too, which records your other expert meetings.
notes.after: On 9 July 2026 we asked Yuan Chiu-Ying, researcher at Cheng Han Biotechnology, how a cell-free protein product is classified in Taiwan and the EU. She said [answer]. For our cell-free output this meant [consequence], so we [change]. We used her briefing as an industry view beside the primary sources.
notes.excerpt_note: Both WageningenUR passages run the full entry in under 150 words, ending with what the team changed.
notes.ballot: How well did it incorporate different stakeholder views?

notes.anchor: BoPEP4, AtLEA14, and ACCD are being developed to address complementary abiotic stresses
notes.title: Two spellings of the same peptide
notes.body: This page writes BoPEP4 seven times and BoPep4 three times. Every other ReLeaf page writes BoPep4. Change all of them to BoPep4 and search the page for the other spelling.
notes.after: BoPep4, AtLEA14, and ACCD are being developed to address complementary abiotic stresses.

notes.anchor: Organic production standards may restrict genetically modified organisms and certain inputs.
notes.title: Organic rules are stricter than this
notes.body: The Geospatial Analysis page states it as a hard exclusion: "Taiwan's Organic Agriculture Promotion Act excludes any product of a genetically modified organism from certified organic production, regardless of containment", and puts the lost land at about 3.7%. Your row says standards "may restrict". Name the Act here and state the exclusion, since it is a market limit a judge will look for.
notes.after: Taiwan's Organic Agriculture Promotion Act excludes any product of a genetically modified organism from certified organic production, whatever the containment. Certified organic farming is therefore closed to ReLeaf, about 3.7% of cultivated land.

notes.anchor: Final TSCA Part 725 pathway remains to be determined
notes.title: Give each open item an owner
notes.body: This table is the strongest section on the page, and every row stops at the problem. Add two columns: who you would ask, and the next step with a date. An open question with a plan reads as work in progress.
notes.after: Issue: US engineered culture. Status: final TSCA Part 725 pathway undetermined. Who we would ask: [body]. Next step: [action] by [date].
notes.excerpt_note: UZurich gives a pending rule its deadline and its current status in two sentences.
notes.ballot: To what extent is the Human Practices work documented so that others can build upon it?

notes.anchor: regulatory strategy can therefore be reduced to five questions
notes.title: Move these five questions up
notes.body: These are the best lines on the page, and they arrive last. Put them at the top, as the questions the page answers, and let section 11 give the answers. A reader can then hold every section against a question.
notes.after: (Open the page with the five questions, then answer them in order: What does ReLeaf do? What will we claim? Which category could contain those claims? What requirements follow? Is the market practical?)
notes.excerpt_note: Both winners open with the questions their page then answers in order.

notes.anchor: Promulgated June 16, 1999; last amended June 19, 2002
notes.title: Add article numbers and real links
notes.body: Your references give bare domains, and no claim in the text carries an article number. Put the article beside each claim, give the full link and the date you read it, and add an "as of" date for rules still changing, such as Indonesia's PP No. 7/2026. Your casebook found no winning page that does this, so it is the cheapest way for your page to stand out.
notes.after: Ministry of Agriculture, Taiwan. Fertilizer Management Act, Article [n] (promulgated 16 June 1999, last amended 19 June 2002). [full URL], accessed [date].
notes.excerpt_note: Waterloo's numbered, dated government references are the minimum; the article number next to the claim is the part you can beat them on.
notes.ballot: To what extent is the Human Practices work documented so that others can build upon it?
